summary: Canary qualifier probe sequence out-of-order breaks version affinity and triggers mixed-model fallback
description:
Issue summary:

Customer FinSight Labs reported intermittent mixed-generation outputs after a scheduled canary promotion on their dedicated capacity pool in us-east. Customer had pinned production route to open-llama-13b-quant-v1 but observed ~2-5% of requests temporarily routed to v2 and to a degraded fallback variant during the canary window.

Impact:
- Affecting ~3k requests/min for the customer during the canary window (P1 business impact).
- Some user sessions received inconsistent outputs (different model behaviors) and transient latency spikes (p50 doubled for affected requests).

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (g5dn-like) serving FinSight Labs tenant in us-east.
- Route config: model pin to v1, canary slice enabled (5% weight), prewarm probes enabled with immediate qualifier probe sequence.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule a weighted canary promoting open-llama-13b-quant-v2 to 5% while keeping route pinned to v1.
2) Enable prewarm + qualifier probes (default immediate sequence).
3) Observe through customer telemetry and SDK traces over 10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- During prewarm and qualifier window, some requests had model affinity flip to v2 or a degraded fallback for a short window (~20-90s) despite the explicit pin.
- Edge and orchestrator traces show qualifier probe ACKs arriving out-of-order relative to probe dispatch; snapshot commit for cohort reassigned before the pin handshake completed.

Expected behavior:
- Prewarm/qualifier probes should preserve explicit pin for pinned routes; probe ACK ordering should not cause a cohort snapshot commit that rebinds routing cohorts mid-handshake.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Orchestrator logs (orchestrator-2026-03-10-13:22) show probe_ack timestamps: 13:22:03 -> probe for v2, 13:22:02 -> probe for v1 (out-of-order), with commit id mismatch 0x1f4a/0x1f4b.
- Edge traces (edge-proxy-us-east-3) show X-Canary-Qualifier: seq=42, seq=41 for concurrent probes.
- Console: token-level latency spike correlated to probe window.
- Customer supplied SDK logs: request_ids: [finsight-req-00023, finsight-req-00047].
comments: 2026-03-10 13:35 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged receipt. Opening investigation with SRE and Eng. Provided customer temporary mitigation steps (disabled prewarm qualifier).

2026-03-10 14:10 - SRE (Marco Chen): Reproduced ordering anomaly in staging when prewarm probe fanout > 20. Observed ack reorder under burst probe fanout. Collecting orchestrator and edge pcap for root cause.

2026-03-11 09:02 - Eng (Lena Ortiz): Hypothesis: orchestrator probe scheduler uses parallel workers that don't preserve logical sequence IDs under retry/backpressure; snapshot commit path doesn't verify in-flight handshake for pinned cohorts. Creating PR to enforce in-order ack handling.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Customer (J. Alvarez, FinSight): Confirmed that disabling qualifier probe eliminated mixed outputs during the next canary test. Wants ETA for permanent fix and asks about retroactive billing impact from degraded fallback calls.
investigation_notes: Collected packet captures and orchestrator trace logs from us-east nodes for the 13:20-13:25 window.
Found that when probe concurrency exceeded worker pool size, ack responses were processed by different ack-handlers without seq check, allowing later probes to commit earlier probe's snapshot (race).
(Related) observed prewarm mirror on standby nodes sometimes replied before primary edge due to cached mirror state, creating perceived out-of-order ACKs.
Reproduced in internal load test: enabled canary qualifier with 50 concurrent prewarm probes -> ~4% of traffic experienced transient cohort rebind and fallback to degraded variant.
Telemetry: cohort_snapshot_commit_rate increased with probe concurrency; commit rollback events tied to commit id mismatch logs.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-10 15:00): disabled qualifier probes for FinSight route and set canary_weight to 0 temporarily. Patch deployed to staging (orchestrator PR 6789) that adds seq validation to probe-ack path and holds commit until handshake completion. Patch rolled to prod us-east on 2026-03-12 02:20 behind a staged rollout (staged by region). Monitoring shows no recurrence in follow-up tests. Billing: fallback requests were within committed reserved capacity; CS to coordinate with finance if customer requests credit. Follow-ups: full postmortem and recommended change to prewarm concurrency default (reduce default fanout and add in-order ack enforcement).
next_steps: Complete postmortem and share with customer (owner: Marco Chen) by 2026-03-18
Adjust default prewarm qualifier fanout and add a config toggle to force sequential prewarm for pinned routes (owner: Release Eng)
Add automated test that simulates high probe concurrency and asserts commit id monotonicity (owner: Test Infra)
CS to open billing review if FinSight requests credit (owner: Rachel Moore)
Link permanent fix PR to changelog and release notes for Dedicated customers (owner: Product)
